title: Change set
description: A proposed mutation, defined as a contract with no execution path in v1 (FR-06, CON-02). The schema exists so that a future mutation has a reviewed shape to fill; nothing in this framework consumes it. Non-existence of an execution path is asserted statically over declared core paths, because exercising behaviour cannot prove absence (SEC-012, NEG-H). This artifact is deliberately distinct from any diagnostic output, which is what FR-57 means by separating read-only findings from proposed mutations.

scopeContractHash.description: The canonical hash of the scope contract this proposal was produced under. Binding to the hash rather than the name is what makes a proposal written against a since-changed scope detectable instead of silently re-interpreted.

lifecycleState.description: No executed state exists. That absence is the contract-level expression of 'no execution path in v1': a change set cannot even represent having been applied, so no artifact can claim it was. Adding such a state is a deliberate schema change that a reviewer will see, not a configuration choice (FR-06, FR-58).

preconditions.description: What must hold before this could be applied. Non-empty: a proposal asserting no preconditions is asserting it is safe under every condition, which is a claim nobody can review.

blastRadius.description: What this would touch and whether it can be undone. Required in full, because a proposal whose blast radius is unstated is one whose risk was never assessed.

affectedScopeEntries.description: Selectors naming what would be affected, drawn from the scope contract. Placeholders only in any shipped example.

reversible.description: Stated explicitly. An irreversible proposal is permitted to exist and must announce itself, so that the approval decision is taken knowing which kind it is.

rollbackPlan.description: Required even when the proposal is reversible, because 'reversible in principle' and 'reversible by a named sequence within a known time' are different claims.

maximumRollbackSeconds.description: The upper bound on returning to the prior state. Bounded so that the rollback plan carries a commitment rather than an intention.

verificationMethod.description: How anyone would know the change did what it claimed. Without a success criterion, verification degrades to 'it did not obviously fail'.

canonicalHash.description: SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 canonical form of this document with this property removed, lowercase hex (ADR-0004). The approval ledger references this value, so approving a proposal and then editing it produces a hash that no longer matches the approval.

schemaVersion.description: The version of this schema the instance conforms to (FR-05, FR-29). Pinned with const rather than left to the pattern: without it an instance could declare any version at all and still validate, which made the declaration decorative (NFR-21).

identifier.description: Lowercase, hyphen-separated. Constrained so an identifier cannot carry arbitrary text, and English by construction (FR-03, CON-01).

timestamp.description: RFC 3339, UTC, Z-suffixed. The pattern is present because format is an annotation by default.

sha256Hex.description: Lowercase hex, exactly 64 characters, as ADR-0004 pins.

statement.description: One reviewable sentence. Bounded above so a step cannot become an essay that nobody reads.
